title: Agent Context Memory (ACM): A Governance-First Specification
description:
What this is. Agent Context Memory (ACM) is a governance-first specification for how AI-assisted work is kept organised in memory separate from repositories of work. A team use is called Shared ACM; the same model serves one person or an organisation.

Contribution. ACM treats agent memory as an authorization problem. Its Mandate Gate requires principal-confirmed intent before governed work. Memory is organised into Intent, Trace, and Evidence tiers; work repositories bind to repository-level scopes by identity; and 21 numbered requirements specify checks for authority, append-only recording, independent evidence, scoped retrieval, and bounded startup cost.

v0.9.0 release. This version restores Agent Context Memory as the canonical public specification name. Shared ACM describes a team use, not a separate specification. The 21 requirements, their checks, and their Proposed status are unchanged. Earlier SACM releases and citations remain historical records.

Relationship to PEA. ACM implements the Principles of Earned Autonomy (PEA) for the context-memory design problem. It can be used independently of the author's implementations. Agent Evidence Proxy can supply an external evidence boundary, but ACM claims no implementation conformance.

Claims and limitations. Every requirement is Proposed. The specification does not claim that any named implementation is conformant, that a hash chain prevents full-ledger rewriting, or that model reasoning itself is made correct. It acknowledges CoALA, Generative Agents, MemGPT, RBAC/MAC, and audit-log prior art.

Read in this order. README.md, then SPEC.md.
notes: Versions up to 0.5.0 were published as Agent Context Memory (ACM); versions 0.7.0 through 0.8.0 were published as Shared Agent Context Memory (SACM). v0.9.0 restores ACM as the specification name and uses Shared ACM only for a team use of it. Historical titles and citations remain unchanged. Version 0.7.1 changes only that record's metadata and version/date strings; version 0.8.0 renamed mission.md to goal.md. v0.9.0 changes identity and release metadata, not the 21 requirements or their Proposed status.
